analyst_view.overall: Early view: a relegation scrap between Regis Le Bris's Sunderland (19th, 8 points) and Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest (16th, 9 points), both of whom won last time out, Sunderland 1-0 against Chelsea and Forest 3-1 against Manchester City. Sunderland play AC Milan away in the Europa League on Thursday 10 December, so they will have tired legs and possible rotation; I found no European game for Forest that week.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: in a game this tense, both sides may play not to lose, and Forest under Glasner sit deep and counter (they had 22% of the ball against City) while conceding few chances. Sunderland's win over Chelsea came from a single penalty by Enzo Le Fee.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Sunderland at home should have more of the ball and will cross a lot, which brings corners, but fatigue after Milan may limit their pressure, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: points matter a great deal at the bottom, and Forest's counter-attacking approach tends to draw tactical fouls from the side that has the ball. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots. I lean lower: Forest are happy to give up possession and wait for openings, and a Sunderland side three days after a trip to Milan may lack the energy for a high-volume game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I lean a little lower for the same reasons: a cagey game with Forest defending deep and few clear chances at either end.
